fluff.overview:
The Sasquatch was introduced in 3054 as the Vining Engineering and Salvage Team's ambitious entry into the assault 'Mech market. Designed on Solaris VII by one of the game world's most innovative independent design firms, the eighty-five-ton Sasquatch was originally conceived as an arena combatant capable of dominating gladiatorial combat at the highest weight classes. VEST had built a reputation on smaller, unconventional designs, and the Sasquatch represented a significant leap in scale and ambition for the company.

Despite the spectacle of its public debut and VEST's considerable marketing efforts, the Sasquatch never achieved the commercial success its creators envisioned, with sales records showing only limited purchases over the following decades.
fluff.capabilities:
The production Sasquatch centers its firepower around a Grizzard Model 200 Gauss rifle, providing devastating long-range striking power that few arena opponents can match. This primary armament is supplemented by three Martell-X medium X-pulse lasers and a single Exostar small laser, giving the 'Mech reliable close-range firepower with improved accuracy over standard pulse weapons. A large shield mounted on the left arm provides additional physical protection, allowing MechWarriors to absorb incoming fire while closing to effective engagement range.

The heart of the Sasquatch is its EXP 425 XXL engine, an experimental extra-extra-light fusion plant that saves considerable weight but introduces significant vulnerability. The mammoth power plant allows the design to carry its heavy armament and StarSlab Standard armor protection while maintaining respectable mobility for an assault-class chassis. However, the XXL engine's extreme weight savings come at the cost of durability, as damage to either side torso can destroy the engine entirely.

VEST's use of prototype and experimental components throughout the design creates persistent logistical challenges for any force attempting to field the 'Mech outside of Solaris VII's well-stocked parts markets. Maintenance crews unfamiliar with these systems report significantly higher downtime compared to conventional assault designs of similar tonnage.
fluff.history:
The Sasquatch's origins lie in VEST's decision during the mid-3050s to expand beyond the medium and heavy weight classes that had built the firm's reputation on Solaris VII. Having already achieved commercial success with designs like the Jackal, and having parlayed their front-line observations during the initial Clan Invasion into innovative new technologies, VEST's engineers set their sights on producing a competitive assault-class arena 'Mech.

Development of the Sasquatch was disrupted in 3054 when a recently hired technician absconded with the SQS-TH-001 prototype during a shakedown run, delivering it to the Vampire Stables. Rather than attempt to recover the machine through conventional means, VEST challenged the Vampires to an arena duel for possession of the stolen prototype. The resulting match in the King of the Mountain arena saw the hastily completed second prototype soundly defeat the stolen original, effectively destroying both machines in the process. The event generated considerable publicity and drew immediate interest from spectators, with several individuals placing sizable orders in the aftermath.

Despite this dramatic debut, the Sasquatch struggled to find a market beyond the arenas of Solaris VII. VEST's projections for the new assault 'Mech proved overly optimistic, as public sales records over the following decade showed consistently poor performance. Rumors persisted of significant purchases by the Word of Blake, though verifiable records showed only lackluster sales to Solaris VII stables. The design entered production as the SQS-TH-002 in 3065, incorporating updated technology in an effort to revitalize commercial interest.

The Word of Blake's occupation of Solaris VII during the Jihad devastated VEST's operations along with virtually every other manufacturer on the game world. VEST pledged their support to the Solaris Home Defense League during the fighting, and their facilities sustained extensive damage in the prolonged conflict. In the aftermath, rather than selling off their designs from a position of weakness, VEST pursued an initial public offering on the Lyran Alliance Stock Exchange in 3079 to fund rebuilding and staff recruitment. The Sasquatch's limited production history and the destruction wrought by the Jihad left few examples of the design in active service, making it a rare sight even on the arenas where it was born.
fluff.deployment: The original SQS-TH-001 was the first Sasquatch prototype, mounting a more conventional VOX 340 extra-light engine paired with jump jets to compensate for the slower ground speed. Armed with a Gauss rifle, four medium pulse lasers, a small laser, twin machine guns, and an anti-missile system, the prototype carried a broader weapon loadout than the production model at the cost of roughly a ton less armor protection. The SQS-TH-001 gained notoriety when it was stolen from VEST's Xolara facility by a hired infiltrator working for the Vampire Stables, leading directly to the development of the superior SQS-TH-002. The stolen prototype was ultimately destroyed in an arena duel against the redesigned Sasquatch.
